production.waterSource: The distillery sits on a Kentucky River limestone shelf and uses limestone-filtered local water, which naturally removes iron before mashing.
production.malt: Wild Turkey uses non-GMO corn, rye and malted barley across its bourbon and rye mash bills.
production.fermentation: A proprietary yeast strain is used in a sour-mash process. Campari technical material identifies 23 fermenters and an approximately 80-90 hour fermentation, producing a beer around 10% ABV.
production.stills: The main distillation system uses a tall 19-plate column still followed by a doubler/pot-style second distillation. Wild Turkey deliberately distils at a lower proof than the legal maximum to retain more flavour and reduce subsequent dilution.
production.maturation: New make enters new charred American white-oak barrels at a deliberately low proof; the house uses No. 4 char barrels and matures in Kentucky warehouses under the Russell family's long-standing production regime.

houseCharacter: Wild Turkey combines high-rye grain recipes, a proprietary yeast culture and relatively long sour-mash fermentation to generate a robust, spicy ferment before distillation. The 19-plate column and doubler are operated at deliberately lower proof than the legal ceiling, retaining more congeners and reducing the amount of water needed before barrel entry. Heavy-char American oak then amplifies vanilla, caramel and spice without erasing the grain-driven structure.
cask23Narrative: Wild Turkey's flavour starts with a production philosophy of keeping more character rather than stripping it away. Limestone water, a proprietary yeast strain and long sour-mash fermentation feed a column-and-doubler system that deliberately distils below the legal maximum proof. The whiskey then enters heavily charred American oak at a relatively low proof, helping explain the dense spice, caramel and grain intensity associated with the house style.
